transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (CTO, Glyph), Luis Ortega (DevOps), Danielle Price (Security), Tom Reed (ML Engineer)

Summary section (auto): Quick discovery focused on network topology for private deployment, security requirements, and region placement. Next steps agreed around docs and a benchmark run.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving time. quick intros?
[00:14] Samira: Hi I'm Samira, CTO at Glyph, we build financial analytics models, exploring Redwood private option because of data residency and compliance.
[00:23] Luis: Luis, DevOps, I'll be implementing network stuff.
[00:27] Danielle: Danielle, security, SOC2 and KMS questions up front.
[00:31] Tom: Tom, ML engineer, will run the tests with Ethan.
[00:35] Maya: Great. Ethan and I are Redwood — Ethan's our SE and will dig into network/benchmarks.
[00:42] Ethan: Hey all. quick overview: Redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC) — private can be VPC peering or private endpoint depending on cloud. today we'll focus on your requirements.
[01:05] Samira: High-level: we need private control plane or at least no public egress for inference payloads; EU data residency for some datasets, but we also have US customers — so multi-region or cross-region concerns. also want audit logs, SSO, RBAC.
[01:30] Maya: Totally. for Private we offer a customer-managed VPC with a control-plane connection — there are two common patterns: VPC peering/transit gateway where our nodes live in your VPC, or PrivateLink/Private Endpoint where we provide an interface endpoint and you allow access. each has trade-offs.
[01:52] Luis: can you expand on the pros/cons? we have strict CIDR ranges and some overlapping addresses with partners, transit gateway is in use.
[02:05] Ethan: Sure. Peering/transit gateway gives you full L3 access, easier to use existing route tables and security groups, and the compute nodes can be in your subnets — lower latency. downside is cross-account peering setup and potential CIDR overlap. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) avoids CIDR overlap but requires NAT for egress to model artifact stores unless we place S3 endpoints. PrivateLink also means we manage the compute in our VPC and you connect via endpoints.
[02:34] Danielle: BYOK? we need keys in our KMS/HSM — can Redwood integrate with our KMS or do we need BYOK?
[02:45] Ethan: We support BYOK and KMS integrations for both data plane and control plane metadata. for HSM-level certs we have options — we can surface a customer-managed key for encryption at rest and integrate with Cloud KMS/HSM providers. we'll need to capture exact key policies though.
[03:10] Tom: What's the network egress behavior? our models fetch artifacts from our S3 buckets and we push logs to our ELK.
[03:19] Maya: In peering mode the compute nodes have your VPC egress — so artifact access is within your network. with PrivateLink we may require a controlled egress path to your storage or reciprocal endpoints. we'll map that out.
[03:35] Luis: we use AWS in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. can Redwood run inference in both regions?
[03:42] Ethan: Yes, we can deploy regionally. private control plane has to be in the same region as the compute typically; multi-region deployment is possible but adds orchestration for model sync and replication. latency between regions will be a factor.
[04:05] Samira: Are there pre-built network diagrams or a checklist for our network team?
[04:12] Maya: yes, we'll send the private deployment checklist and a sample network diagram. it shows required subnets, route table entries, security group ports (gRPC/HTTPS), and required NAT/endpoint configs.
[04:27] Danielle: audit logs and retention? we need 12 months of immutable logs for compliance.
[04:33] Ethan: Redwood provides audit logs from the control plane; for data plane logs we can forward to your logging endpoint (we've done S3/CloudWatch/Kafka). retention can be configured; immutable WORM retention we can support via your object-store policies.
[04:52] Luis: CIDR overlap scenario — we have a partner network that overlaps. is there a recommended approach?
[05:00] Ethan: If overlap exists, PrivateLink is safer. alternatively, use NAT and route isolation, or reserved overlay CIDR with transit gateway translations, but that's more ops. PrivateLink avoids L3 overlap because it's an interface endpoint L4/L7.
[05:20] Tom: How about egress IPs and allowlisting? we'll need a static set of IPs to whitelist for outbound callbacks.
[05:29] Maya: For dedicated/private we can provide static egress IPs for the control-plane callbacks or support a NAT gateway inside your VPC so outbound IPs come from your NAT. if you want Redwood-managed egress we can provide an IP range but it's easier if you manage NAT.
[05:50] Samira: Security: SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC?
[05:55] Ethan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, role-based access controls in the console, and audit trails for token usage. we'll add the SAML metadata exchange in the docs.
[06:15] Luis: Any requirements on route tables and ports? we lock down egress via NACLs.
[06:21] Ethan: Minimum is HTTPS (443) for API, and gRPC ports for high throughput depending on setup; if compute sits in your subnets we'll list exact ports. health checks and metrics endpoints may be required on specific allowlist ranges.
[06:40] Maya: let's talk about capacity model — you mentioned expected throughput?
[06:45] Samira: We're looking at 200 concurrent short chats during market hours and batch embedding jobs off-hours. token sizes vary — typically 256-512 tokens per request.
[06:56] Ethan: For that workload we recommend a mix: private deployment with dedicated GPU pools pinned to your account, autoscaling policy for peak. We'll provide throughput per-GPU numbers in the benchmark doc.
[07:12] Tom: Do you support quantized models to reduce GPU memory?
[07:16] Ethan: Yes, runtime supports quantization profiles and we can recommend a quantized variant to hit lower-cost profiles. quality monitoring tied to prompt sets will detect regressions.
[07:30] Samira: Latency SLOs? we need <200ms 95th for short prompts.
[07:36] Ethan: That depends on model and sequence length. For a smaller model in-region on pinned GPUs that's achievable; for larger models or cross-region you'd see higher tails. our benchmarks will show 95/99 latencies.
[07:55] Luis: VPN/Direct Connect options? we use Direct Connect for private links to partners.
[08:02] Maya: We support setup over Direct Connect or VPN; Direct Connect is preferred for consistent bandwidth. we'll include a Direct Connect design note.
[08:18] Danielle: Data residency: some datasets must remain in the EU. can you ensure model weights or logs aren't replicated to the US?
[08:28] Ethan: Yes, we can pin models and data to a region and disable cross-region replication for that customer's workspace. control-plane metadata may be replicated depending on architecture, but we can provide an offering where control plane is private in your region. we'll capture exact requirements in the next step.
[08:55] Samira: Anything about certified connectors to our S3 (encryption in transit at least)?
[09:02] Ethan: We use TLS for transport; for S3 we recommend VPC endpoints or S3 gateway endpoints so traffic never leaves the AWS backbone. we can also support signed URLs if needed.
[09:18] Tom: benchmark plan — how will we measure cost/latency?
[09:22] Ethan: We'll give a test harness that can replay your workload (payload distribution, token distribution). we'll deploy a small pool in your VPC or connect via PrivateLink and run sample workloads. that will produce cost per 1k tokens and latency percentiles.
[09:40] Maya: ok let's talk schedule — we'd like security docs to move quickly. Danielle, what's your timeline?
[09:46] Danielle: We need to review docs this week and decide whether to proceed to pilot next week.
[09:52] Maya: Great. we'll send SOC2, architecture diagrams, network checklist, and initial cost model.
[10:00] Samira: A few nitty-gritty questions: how are updates to models handled? who controls rollouts?
[10:07] Ethan: Rollouts can be controlled by you — pin to model versions and we have canary rollouts and A/Bs. for private deployments we'll coordinate upgrades; by default we won't auto-upgrade model servings without an agreed window.
[10:24] Luis: On the peering setup, we have multiple accounts per team. will Redwood require cross-account peering?
[10:31] Ethan: Typically you create a dedicated network account where Redwood peering goes, or we support cross-account endpoints. we'll outline both in the design doc.
[10:45] Tom: Observability: can we get per-route latency and token-level cost breakdown?
[10:50] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, tracing hooks, and exportable traces.
[11:00] Samira: Any regulatory constraints we should be aware of? GLBA/FINRA?
[11:06] Danielle: we're in fintech, so everything is sensitive; we need audit, strong key control, and retention policies.
[11:12] Ethan: We have enterprise packages with extended log retention, dedicated compliance options, and support for customer-managed keys.
[11:28] Luis: network team will want a runbook for failover — if region is down, can traffic failover to another region but keep data controls?
[11:37] Ethan: We can set up cross-region fallbacks, but if strict data residency is required you might not allow failover. typically we configure fallback to a nearby region and disable sensitive dataset replication.
[11:59] Maya: let's go through a quick demo of the network diagram — Ethan?
[12:05] Ethan: (shares screen) here's diagram A: peering mode — compute nodes in your subnets, route table entries we require, security groups open between subnets for gRPC, metrics forwarded to your CloudWatch. here's diagram B: PrivateLink — interface endpoint in your account pointing to our service endpoint. note the differences in egress and artifact access.
[12:40] Tom: I'm seeing a note about NAT and S3 access in PrivateLink diagram. if we use VPC endpoint to S3 is that sufficient?
[12:47] Ethan: yes, VPC endpoint to S3 ensures artifacts access stays private. multiple endpoints for KMS might be needed depending on keys.
[12:58] Samira: how long to get a pilot running?
[13:03] Maya: once we get network configs and a security review signed off, typical pilot is 2-4 weeks to provision and run benchmarks.
[13:12] Danielle: what's included in the pilot?
[13:15] Ethan: small dedicated pool, model pinning, benchmarks (latency/cost), security review, and runbook for production cutover.
[13:28] Luis: about throughput — we need 200 concurrent chats, what GPU types do you recommend?
[13:35] Ethan: depends on model size — for smaller Llama-type models A100 or H100 depending on batching. we'll propose a couple of profiles in the follow-up.
[13:47] Tom: Any limits on network throughput from the instances? we have 10Gb links.
[13:52] Ethan: network throughput is tied to instance types; we can size accordingly.
[14:03] Samira: backup question — where are logs stored for the control plane?
[14:10] Maya: control-plane logs are stored in our managed account but are available via export; for full compliance we can ship logs to your S3 bucket.
[14:22] Danielle: is there an SOC2 attestation we can review?
[14:25] Maya: yes we'll attach our SOC2 report in the email.
[14:30] Luis: any AWS principals or IAM roles we need to create?
[14:35] Ethan: we'll give an IAM role template for cross-account access where needed.
[14:42] Samira: What's the pricing model for private? is it reserved capacity + infra?
[14:48] Maya: Private is typically pricing with a platform fee plus reserved capacity for dedicated GPUs and usage tiers. we'll include an indicative quote.
[14:57] Tom: for the benchmark, do you need sample data? we can scrub and provide synthetic workflows.
[15:02] Ethan: synthetic representative workflows are perfect; if you can provide token distribution and example prompts that's ideal.
[15:12] Samira: okay, timeline-wise our security review this week, and then pilot next.
[15:18] Maya: perfect. action items recap now?
[15:22] Maya: Ethan, you'll own the benchmark. Luis will share network details. Danielle will confirm KMS/HSM constraints. I'll send security and architecture docs.
[15:32] Ethan: noted. I'll prepare the harness and schedule an on-site or remote run.
[15:38] Danielle: one more question — backups and disaster recovery for model weights?
[15:44] Ethan: weights can be stored in your object store or in encrypted snapshots; DR procedures can be included in the runbook.
[15:52] Samira: thanks, this was helpful.
[15:55] Luis: thanks all.
[15:58] Maya: we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. talk soon.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "PrivateLink" was sometimes transcribed as "private linke", names may be slightly off. Speaker labels approximate.)
